items.q: Which of the following statements best describes a primary objective of testing?

o.A: Proving that the software contains no remaining defects
o.B: Preventing defects by evaluating work products such as requirements and designs
o.C: Producing the highest possible failure rate so developers can be assessed
o.D: Giving stakeholders full certainty that the product is free of bugs

items.exEn: Testing is not only dynamic execution: evaluating work products early prevents defects before they reach the code.
items.qAr: أي عبارة تصف بشكل أفضل أحد الأهداف الرئيسية للاختبار؟
items.exAr: الاختبار ليس تنفيذاً للكود فقط؛ تقييم مخرجات العمل مبكراً يمنع الـ defects قبل أن تصل إلى الكود.

items.q: What is the key difference between testing and debugging?

o.A: Testing reveals failures caused by defects, while debugging locates, analyzes and fixes the cause
o.B: Testing is performed only by developers, while debugging is performed only by testers
o.C: Testing prevents defects, while debugging checks whether requirements are satisfied
o.D: Testing is a reactive activity, while debugging is a preventive quality assurance activity

items.exEn: Dynamic testing shows failures caused by defects; debugging is the development activity that finds, fixes and verifies the cause.
items.qAr: ما الفرق الرئيسي بين الـ testing والـ debugging؟
items.exAr: الاختبار الديناميكي يُظهر الأعطال الناتجة عن الـ defects، بينما الـ debugging نشاط تطويري يحدد السبب ويصلحه ويتحقق من الإصلاح.

items.q: Why is testing necessary in software development?

o.A: It ensures the software will never experience an operational failure
o.B: It completely replaces code reviews and architecture inspections
o.C: It reduces the risk of failure during operation and helps satisfy contractual and regulatory requirements
o.D: It guarantees that the software is released ahead of schedule

items.exEn: Testing lowers risk, gives information about quality, and can be required by contracts or regulations.
items.qAr: لماذا يُعدّ الاختبار ضرورياً في تطوير البرمجيات؟
items.exAr: الاختبار يقلل المخاطر ويوفّر معلومات عن الجودة، وقد يكون مطلوباً تعاقدياً أو تنظيمياً.

items.q: Which testing principle states that testing can show that defects are present, but cannot prove that there are no defects?

o.A: Exhaustive testing is impossible
o.B: Defects cluster together
o.C: The absence-of-errors fallacy
o.D: Testing shows the presence of defects, not their absence

items.exEn: This principle states that testing reduces the probability of undiscovered defects but can never prove correctness.
items.qAr: أي مبدأ من مبادئ الاختبار ينص على أن الاختبار يُظهر وجود الـ defects ولا يمكنه إثبات عدم وجودها؟
items.exAr: هذا المبدأ ينص على أن الاختبار يقلل احتمال وجود defects غير مكتشفة، لكنه لا يثبت خلو النظام منها.

items.q: What is meant by the principle 'Exhaustive testing is impossible'?

o.A: Testing every combination of inputs and preconditions is not feasible except in trivial cases
o.B: Automated tools cannot execute more than a fixed number of test cases per day
o.C: Testing all combinations is feasible only for safety-critical systems
o.D: Testing must stop as soon as the project budget is used up

items.exEn: Except for trivial software, the number of input and precondition combinations is far too large to cover; risk and priorities guide the effort instead.
items.qAr: ما المقصود بمبدأ «الاختبار الشامل مستحيل» (exhaustive testing is impossible)؟
items.exAr: باستثناء الحالات البسيطة جداً، عدد تركيبات المدخلات والشروط المسبقة أكبر من أن يُغطّى، لذا تُوجَّه الجهود حسب المخاطر والأولويات.

items.q: Which of the following describes the 'Absence-of-errors fallacy'?

o.A: Assuming that finding and fixing defects guarantees success even if the system is unusable
o.B: Assuming developers will not introduce defects if static analysis is performed
o.C: Assuming that finding no defects means the system fits user needs and business goals
o.D: Assuming automated tests will detect every regression

items.exEn: Even a defect-free build fails if it does not meet user needs and business objectives.
items.qAr: أي مما يلي يصف مغالطة «غياب الأخطاء» (absence-of-errors fallacy)؟
items.exAr: حتى النسخة الخالية من الـ defects تفشل إذا لم تلبِّ احتياجات المستخدمين وأهداف الأعمال.

items.q: What is the relationship between an error, a defect, and a failure?

o.A: A failure made by a developer causes an error, which results in a defect
o.B: A human error introduces a defect in the work product, and executing that defect may cause a failure
o.C: A defect leads to an error, which then produces an operational failure
o.D: An error is an operational flaw, while a failure is a flaw in the design documentation

items.exEn: Error (human mistake) → defect (in code or document) → failure (observed during execution).
items.qAr: ما العلاقة بين الـ error والـ defect والـ failure؟
items.exAr: خطأ بشري (error) ← يُنتج defect في الكود أو الوثيقة ← قد يؤدي إلى عطل (failure) أثناء التنفيذ.

items.q: Which of the following is a key activity in the ISTQB test process?

o.A: Writing the production application code
o.B: Negotiating the customer contract
o.C: Procuring the hardware for the servers
o.D: Test planning and test completion

items.exEn: The test process covers planning, monitoring and control, analysis, design, implementation, execution and completion.
items.qAr: أي مما يلي يُعدّ نشاطاً أساسياً في عملية الاختبار وفقاً لـ ISTQB؟
items.exAr: تشمل عملية الاختبار: التخطيط، المراقبة والتحكم، التحليل، التصميم، التنفيذ الفعلي والإعداد له، ثم الإنهاء.

items.q: What is the primary role of 'Test Analysis' in the test process?

o.A: Determining HOW the tests will be executed
o.B: Creating the execution schedule and assigning testers
o.C: Writing the automated test scripts
o.D: Determining WHAT to test by identifying and prioritizing test conditions

items.exEn: Test analysis examines the test basis to identify testable features and derive test conditions.
items.qAr: ما الدور الرئيسي لـ test analysis في عملية الاختبار؟
items.exAr: يحلل الـ test analysis أساس الاختبار لتحديد الخصائص القابلة للاختبار واشتقاق شروط الاختبار.

items.q: Which activity is performed during 'Test Design'?

o.A: Elaborating test conditions into test cases and other testware
o.B: Evaluating the testability of the requirements
o.C: Assembling test suites and preparing the test data and environment
o.D: Logging defect reports in a tracking tool

items.exEn: Test design answers HOW to test by turning test conditions into concrete test cases and test data requirements.
items.qAr: ما النشاط الذي يُنفَّذ خلال مرحلة الـ test design؟
items.exAr: يجيب الـ test design عن «كيف نختبر» بتحويل شروط الاختبار إلى حالات اختبار ومتطلبات بيانات.

items.q: Which skill is essential for a software tester?

o.A: Deep expertise in graphic design
o.B: Authority to approve legal contracts
o.C: Expertise in network cabling infrastructure
o.D: Critical thinking combined with domain knowledge

items.exEn: Testers need critical thinking, curiosity, attention to detail, communication and domain knowledge.

items.q: What is an advantage of independent testing?

o.A: Independent testers do not need any domain knowledge
o.B: Independent testing removes the need for developer component testing
o.C: Independent testers take ownership of product management decisions
o.D: Independent testers are unbiased and tend to notice different types of defects

items.exEn: Independence brings objectivity and challenges the assumptions made by the authors of the work product.

items.q: Which statement describes the 'Pesticide Paradox'?

o.A: Repeating the same tests will eventually stop finding new defects
o.B: Automated tests always find more defects than manual tests
o.C: Defects are always concentrated in a single module of the application
o.D: Early testing prevents the occurrence of fatal system crashes

items.exEn: Test cases need to be reviewed and revised regularly, and new tests written, to keep finding defects.

items.q: What is the difference between Quality Assurance (QA) and testing?

o.A: QA is dynamic execution, while testing is static review
o.B: QA is performed only after deployment, while testing is performed during development
o.C: QA is done only by external auditors, while testing is done by internal teams
o.D: QA focuses on the process and on preventing defects, while testing is a form of quality control focused on detecting them

items.exEn: QA is process-oriented and preventive; testing is part of quality control and is product-oriented.

items.q: Traceability between the test basis and the test work products helps to:

o.A: Remove the need to keep test execution logs
o.B: Determine test coverage and assess the impact of changes to the requirements
o.C: Guarantee fully automated regression testing
o.D: Shorten the project schedule automatically

items.exEn: Traceability supports coverage analysis, impact analysis, auditability and clearer status reporting.

items.q: In any Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) model, good testing practice dictates that:

o.A: Dynamic test execution begins during requirements gathering
o.B: Every development activity has a corresponding test activity
o.C: Testers review the code only after system integration
o.D: Test design starts only after all coding is complete

items.exEn: Each development activity should be matched by a test activity so that defects are found as early as possible.

items.q: Which of the following is a core principle of shift-left in software testing?

o.A: Postponing acceptance testing until end users request it
o.B: Moving test execution to night shifts to save server resources
o.C: Replacing dynamic functional testing with user surveys
o.D: Starting test activities early in the SDLC so defects are found before the code is executed

items.exEn: Shift-left moves testing activities earlier, including reviews of requirements and designs, to catch defects sooner and cheaper.

items.q: In Agile software development, how are testing activities typically integrated?

o.A: Testing takes place in a separate sprint at the end of the release cycle
o.B: Testing is integrated continuously within each iteration using a whole-team approach
o.C: Testing is performed only by external agencies after deployment
o.D: Testing is skipped when user stories pass developer peer review

items.exEn: Agile relies on a whole-team approach in which testing runs continuously inside every iteration.

items.q: What is the primary focus of component (unit) testing?

o.A: Testing individually testable components or modules in isolation
o.B: Verifying end-to-end business workflows across several external systems
o.C: Assessing system behavior under extreme load
o.D: Verifying installation procedures on the target hardware

items.exEn: Component testing targets components that can be tested separately, such as functions, classes and modules.

items.q: Component integration testing focuses on:

o.A: The resilience of third-party cloud data centers
o.B: User satisfaction with the interface layout
o.C: Backup and disaster recovery procedures
o.D: The interactions and interfaces between integrated components

items.exEn: It verifies the interfaces and interactions between components after they have been tested individually.

items.q: Which test level focuses on verifying that the complete integrated system meets the specified system requirements?

o.A: Component testing
o.B: Component integration testing
o.C: Acceptance testing
o.D: System testing

items.exEn: System testing evaluates the behavior and capabilities of the whole integrated system against system requirements.

items.q: What is the main objective of acceptance testing?

o.A: Finding hidden memory leaks in low-level algorithms
o.B: Establishing confidence that the system is ready for release and meets the business needs
o.C: Verifying that API payloads match the schema specification
o.D: Ensuring code coverage reaches its target across all classes

items.exEn: Acceptance testing builds confidence in release readiness rather than aiming primarily to find defects.

items.q: Which form of acceptance testing is conducted by potential customers at the developing organization's site?

o.A: Alpha testing
o.B: Beta testing
o.C: Operational acceptance testing
o.D: Contractual acceptance testing

items.exEn: Alpha testing happens at the developer's site; beta testing happens at the customer's own site.

items.q: What is functional testing primarily concerned with?

o.A: How fast the system performs a task and how quickly it responds
o.B: What the system should do, based on its functions and user requirements
o.C: How easy the software is to learn and operate
o.D: How easily the software can be moved to another environment

items.exEn: Functional testing evaluates the functions the system should perform — the 'what'.

items.q: Non-functional testing includes evaluating which of the following characteristics?

o.A: Business rules and boundary values
o.B: Acceptance criteria of user stories
o.C: Performance efficiency, usability, security and reliability
o.D: Database column definitions

items.exEn: Non-functional testing measures quality characteristics — how well the system behaves rather than what it does.

items.q: What is the primary purpose of regression testing?

o.A: Verifying that a previously reported defect has been fixed
o.B: Detecting unintended side effects introduced into unchanged parts of the software by recent changes
o.C: Evaluating interface layout options for better accessibility
o.D: Training new testers on the system

items.exEn: Regression testing looks for side effects in areas that were not changed; confirming a specific fix is confirmation testing. .confirmation testing

items.q: What is confirmation testing (re-testing)?

o.A: Re-running the entire test suite on every nightly build
o.B: Reviewing features with business owners to confirm the requirements
o.C: Running load tests to confirm server capacity
o.D: Testing performed after a defect is fixed to confirm that the original defect is resolved

items.exEn: Confirmation testing re-executes the failing test to verify that the reported defect has actually been fixed.

items.q: Maintenance testing is triggered by which of the following events?

o.A: The initial drafting of the software architecture document
o.B: Modification, upgrade, migration or retirement of an existing operational system
o.C: The execution of component tests during initial development
o.D: Hiring new developers in the engineering department

items.exEn: Maintenance testing applies to a system already in operation when it is changed, migrated or retired.

items.q: Impact analysis is used during maintenance testing to:

o.A: Estimate the cost of the maintenance team
o.B: Assess the changes and determine the extent of regression testing required
o.C: Evaluate the response time of the production database
o.D: Generate user manuals automatically

items.exEn: Impact analysis identifies the areas affected by a change so the right amount of regression testing can be planned.

items.q: Which statement about test levels and test types is TRUE?

o.A: Functional testing can be performed only at the system test level
o.B: Regression testing applies exclusively to component testing
o.C: Acceptance testing should never include non-functional evaluation
o.D: Non-functional testing can be performed at every test level

items.exEn: Any test type — functional, non-functional, black-box or white-box — can be applied at any test level.

items.q: What is the effect of DevOps on testing?

o.A: It removes the need for automated continuous integration builds
o.B: It restricts testing to manual user testing performed quarterly
o.C: It replaces quality assurance with system administration
o.D: It promotes automated, continuous testing integrated into the CI/CD pipeline

items.exEn: DevOps relies on continuous integration and delivery, so tests run automatically on every change to give fast feedback.

items.q: Which work products can be evaluated using static testing techniques?

o.A: Executable binaries during system runtime only
o.B: The physical hardware of the network servers
o.C: Requirements specifications, architecture designs, user stories, test cases and source code
o.D: CPU performance under stress conditions

items.exEn: Static testing can evaluate almost any readable work product, without executing the software.

items.q: What is a major advantage of static testing compared to dynamic testing?

o.A: It executes the code faster than dynamic test tools
o.B: It detects defects early, when they are cheaper to fix
o.C: It guarantees full automation coverage
o.D: It removes the need for acceptance testing

items.exEn: Defects found by reviews and static analysis are removed before execution, which is significantly cheaper.

items.q: Which of the following defect types is easier to discover using static testing than dynamic testing?

o.A: Database bottlenecks appearing under heavy load
o.B: Memory leaks that appear after long execution
o.C: Inconsistencies, omissions and contradictions in the requirements
o.D: Hardware driver compatibility crashes

items.exEn: Requirement defects, ambiguities and standard violations are naturally exposed by reviews, not by execution.

items.q: Which review type is informal, has no formal documented process, and is commonly used between peers for quick feedback?

o.A: Inspection
o.B: Technical review
o.C: Walkthrough
o.D: Informal review

items.exEn: An informal review follows no defined process and produces no mandatory documented output.

items.q: Which formal review role leads the review meeting and is responsible for the overall success of the review?

o.A: The facilitator (moderator)
o.B: The author
o.C: The scribe (recorder)
o.D: The management representative

items.exEn: The facilitator runs the meeting, manages the time and mediates between the participants.

items.q: What is the primary role of the scribe (recorder) during a review meeting?

o.A: Recording the findings, defects and open decisions raised during the meeting
o.B: Presenting the document to the review team
o.C: Approving the budget needed to fix the defects
o.D: Running the static analysis tools

items.exEn: The scribe collects the anomalies, decisions and recommendations raised in the meeting.

items.q: Which review type is the most formal, is led by a trained moderator, and uses entry/exit criteria and metrics?

o.A: Walkthrough
o.B: Informal review
o.C: Inspection
o.D: Technical review

items.exEn: Inspection is the most formal review type, based on rules, checklists, defined roles, metrics and entry/exit criteria.

items.q: In a review process, what happens during the individual review (preparation) phase?

o.A: The author fixes all the defects found so far
o.B: The facilitator decides whether the project should continue
o.C: Reviewers examine the work product individually and record potential defects and questions
o.D: The scribe logs the defects into the tracking tool

items.exEn: Each reviewer studies the work product alone and notes anomalies before the review meeting takes place.

items.q: Which factor is critical for the success of reviews in an organization?

o.A: Using review results to evaluate the performance of individual staff
o.B: Eliminating dynamic testing once reviews are in place
o.C: Reviewing only software that has already been deployed
o.D: Clear objectives, active management support and a culture that makes participants feel safe

items.exEn: Reviews succeed when the goals are clear, management supports them, and people are not punished for what is found.

items.q: What is a main characteristic of a walkthrough?

o.A: It is led by the author, who guides participants through the work product to gather feedback
o.B: It is led by an external auditor to evaluate team compliance
o.C: It is an unstructured meeting held without the author
o.D: It is carried out exclusively by static analysis tools

items.exEn: In a walkthrough the author presents the work product and the participants raise questions and comments.

items.q: Which static technique reviews a work product from a specific stakeholder viewpoint, such as end user, maintainer or tester?

o.A: Checklist-based review
o.B: Ad-hoc review
o.C: Perspective-based (role-based) reading
o.D: Decision table review

items.exEn: Perspective-based reading asks each reviewer to evaluate the document as one specific stakeholder would.

items.q: Black-box test techniques are primarily based on:

o.A: Analysis of the internal structure and source code of the system
o.B: The experience and intuition of senior QA engineers
o.C: System architecture diagrams and database schemas
o.D: Analysis of the specified requirements, interfaces and functional specifications, without looking at the code

items.exEn: Black-box techniques derive test cases from the specification, independently of the internal implementation.

items.q: White-box test techniques focus on:

o.A: Business process models and acceptance criteria
o.B: Accessibility standards for the user interface
o.C: The internal structure of the code, its control flows and data flows
o.D: Feedback collected from users during beta testing

items.exEn: White-box techniques derive tests from the internal structure and measure structural coverage.

items.q: Experience-based test techniques rely heavily on:

o.A: Formal decision tables and state transition matrices
o.B: Code coverage measurement tools
o.C: Automated regression execution logs
o.D: The knowledge, background and intuition of the tester

items.exEn: They use the tester's skill, domain knowledge and awareness of likely defects to design tests.

items.q: In equivalence partitioning, partitions are divided into:

o.A: Both valid and invalid partitions
o.B: Valid partitions only
o.C: Invalid partitions only
o.D: Dynamic and static partitions

items.exEn: Equivalence partitioning covers accepted (valid) values and rejected (invalid) values alike.

items.q: An input field accepts integer values from 1 to 10 inclusive. Which values are tested in 2-value Boundary Value Analysis?
items.exEn: 2-value BVA tests each boundary and its closest neighbour outside the partition: 1 and 10 with 0 and 11.

items.q: What is a major strength of decision table testing?

o.A: It provides high statement coverage for object-oriented code
o.B: It systematically captures complex business logic made of combinations of conditions and actions
o.C: It measures the response time of API requests
o.D: It identifies missing database indexes

items.exEn: Decision tables make combinations of conditions explicit, so no important combination is silently missed.

items.q: State transition testing is best suited for systems that:

o.A: Move between different states depending on events and current state
o.B: Contain independent mathematical algorithms with no stored state
o.C: Consist only of static pages with text content
o.D: Process bulk batch files sequentially

items.exEn: The technique models states, events, transitions and actions, so it fits systems whose behavior depends on history.

items.q: In statement testing, what represents 100% statement coverage?

o.A: Executing both outcomes of every decision point
o.B: Executing every executable statement in the code at least once
o.C: Testing every combination of input values in the interface
o.D: Executing a test for every user story in the backlog

items.exEn: Statement coverage counts executable statements exercised at least once, and is weaker than branch coverage.

items.q: If a module achieves 100% branch coverage, what can be guaranteed about statement coverage?

o.A: Statement coverage is exactly 50%
o.B: Statement coverage cannot be determined
o.C: Statement coverage is also 100%
o.D: Statement coverage is 0%

items.exEn: Branch coverage subsumes statement coverage: covering all branches necessarily executes all statements.

items.q: Which statement best describes error guessing?

o.A: Test inputs are selected completely at random
o.B: Tests are derived strictly from deployment diagrams
o.C: It is a mathematical technique for calculating code complexity
o.D: Testers anticipate likely mistakes based on experience and knowledge of common failures

items.exEn: Error guessing uses past experience with defects to target the places where they are most likely to occur.

items.q: Exploratory testing is characterized by:

o.A: Writing all test cases months before the design phase
o.B: Automated execution using commercial tools
o.C: Simultaneous learning, test design and test execution
o.D: Complete reliance on formal requirement specifications

items.exEn: In exploratory testing the tester learns about the product, designs and runs tests at the same time.

items.q: Checklist-based testing involves:

o.A: Designing tests using mathematical combination rules
o.B: Closing completed tickets in the project tool
o.C: Designing and executing tests based on a high-level list of items to be checked
o.D: Compiling the code automatically using build tools

items.exEn: The checklist captures lessons learned and common risks, giving consistent coverage without detailed scripts.

items.q: How do user story acceptance criteria relate to test design?

o.A: They serve as a primary test basis for acceptance and system tests
o.B: They are used only by interface designers
o.C: They replace the need for test conditions
o.D: They apply only to non-functional testing

items.exEn: Acceptance criteria describe the expected behavior, so test cases can be derived directly from them.

items.q: In 3-value Boundary Value Analysis, which values are tested for the range [10, 50]?
items.exEn: 3-value BVA tests each boundary together with the value before it and the value after it.

items.q: Which black-box technique efficiently tests valid and invalid combinations of conditions?

o.A: Decision table testing
o.B: Equivalence partitioning
o.C: Statement testing
o.D: Boundary value analysis

items.exEn: Decision tables are built specifically to handle combinations of conditions and their resulting actions.

items.q: What is the primary objective of white-box test techniques?

o.A: Measuring the usability of the software for non-technical users
o.B: Achieving a defined level of structural coverage of the code and its control flows
o.C: Verifying third-party payment gateway protocols
o.D: Evaluating system behavior against user persona expectations

items.exEn: White-box techniques aim at structural coverage criteria derived from the internal implementation.

items.q: Which of the following is an example of an invalid equivalence partition for a field that accepts ages from 18 to 65?
items.exEn: Values below 18 or above 65 fall outside the accepted range and therefore lie in an invalid partition.

items.q: What is the main advantage of collaboration-based approaches such as ATDD?

o.A: They build a shared understanding of the requirements between business, developers and testers before coding starts
o.B: They remove developers from test execution
o.C: They replace code reviews with end-to-end automated tests
o.D: They guarantee a defect-free release

items.exEn: ATDD brings the three perspectives together to agree on acceptance criteria and examples before development.

items.q: Which statement regarding equivalence partitioning is correct?

o.A: It applies only to numeric input parameters
o.B: It requires full knowledge of the source code
o.C: All members of the same partition are expected to be processed in the same way by the software
o.D: It removes the need for boundary value analysis

items.exEn: Because members of a partition are treated alike, testing one representative value normally suffices.

items.q: How is statement coverage calculated?

o.A: (Passed test cases / total test cases) × 100
o.B: (Fixed defects / total reported defects) × 100
o.C: (Lines of code / total project hours) × 100
o.D: (Executed statements / total executable statements) × 100

items.exEn: Coverage is the proportion of executable statements exercised by the tests, expressed as a percentage.

items.q: When using exploratory testing, test execution is guided by:

o.A: Test charters that define the objectives and scope of the session
o.B: Rigid step-by-step scripts stored in a test management tool
o.C: Automated pipeline triggers
o.D: The project Gantt chart

items.exEn: A charter defines the mission, scope and focus of a time-boxed exploratory session.

items.q: Which factor most influences the choice of test techniques?

o.A: The color scheme of the user interface
o.B: The number of developers working remotely
o.C: The brand of the laptops used by the team
o.D: The type of system, applicable standards, risk level, contractual requirements and tester skills

items.exEn: Technique selection depends on the context: system type, risk, regulations, documentation available and team experience.

items.q: In a state transition diagram, what does a transition represent?

o.A: A static page layout
o.B: A database table definition
o.C: A change from one state to another triggered by an event
o.D: An unhandled exception in the code

items.exEn: A transition links a source state to a target state and is caused by an event, possibly with a resulting action.

items.q: What is the main benefit of using checklist-based testing?

o.A: A guarantee of full statement coverage
o.B: Removing the need for static testing
o.C: Consistent coverage of known checks and common failure modes across sessions and testers
o.D: Removing the need for requirement documentation

items.exEn: The checklist keeps important aspects from being overlooked and keeps coverage repeatable between testers.

items.q: What is the primary purpose of a test strategy?

o.A: Detailing the daily assignments of individual testers
o.B: Tracking the status of defects during a sprint
o.C: Documenting the parameters of individual code functions
o.D: Describing the general, high-level approach to testing across an organization or programme

items.exEn: A test strategy is generic and long-lived; a test plan applies that strategy to one specific project or release.

items.q: What is included in a test plan?

o.A: Source code algorithms and database indexes
o.B: Scope, objectives, schedule, resources, risks and the test approach for a specific test effort
o.C: The salary breakdown of the QA team
o.D: Hardware vendor purchase agreements

items.exEn: The test plan documents what will be tested, how, by whom, when, and under which conditions testing starts and stops.

items.q: Which of the following is an example of an entry criterion for testing?

o.A: The test environment is available and the build has been successfully deployed
o.B: 95% of the planned test cases have passed
o.C: All high-severity defects have been closed
o.D: The test completion report has been signed off

items.exEn: Entry criteria are the conditions that must be met before test execution can meaningfully start.

items.q: Which of the following is an example of an exit criterion for testing?

o.A: The requirements documents have been approved by stakeholders
o.B: The test management tool licences have been renewed
o.C: The planned coverage has been achieved and no high-priority defects remain open
o.D: The development backlog for the sprint has been planned

items.exEn: Exit criteria define when a test activity or level can be considered complete.

items.q: What is the purpose of risk-based testing?

o.A: Giving every test case exactly the same priority
o.B: Allocating and prioritizing test effort according to the assessed product risks
o.C: Calculating compensation for system downtime
o.D: Transferring all project risks to external vendors

items.exEn: Risk analysis decides what to test first, how deeply, and what may be left untested.

items.q: Product risk is defined as:

o.A: A risk related directly to the project schedule or to staff turnover
o.B: A budget overrun caused by delayed hardware delivery
o.C: The possibility that a work product fails to satisfy the functional or non-functional needs of its users
o.D: A shortage of training among team members

items.exEn: Product risk concerns the quality of the deliverable itself, such as wrong calculations or poor performance.

items.q: Project risk is defined as:

o.A: The possibility that a calculation routine produces wrong results
o.B: Vulnerability of the application to injection attacks
o.C: Slow system response time during peak hours
o.D: A risk related to project management, schedule, budget, resources or organizational issues

items.exEn: Project risks threaten the ability to deliver; product risks threaten the quality of what is delivered.

items.q: In software testing, risk level is evaluated as a combination of:

o.A: The likelihood of occurrence and the impact if it occurs
o.B: The execution speed of the tests and the cost of the team
o.C: The number of lines of code and the size of the database
o.D: The sprint duration and the size of the team

items.exEn: Risk level = likelihood × impact, and it drives prioritization of the test effort.

items.q: Which metric provides valuable information about test execution progress?

o.A: The total number of lines of application code written
o.B: The number of meetings held during the sprint
o.C: The percentage of executed test cases that passed, failed or are blocked
o.D: The number of documents stored on the shared drive

items.exEn: Pass, fail and blocked rates against the plan show whether execution is on track.

items.q: What is configuration management primarily responsible for in software testing?

o.A: Managing payroll and employee benefits
o.B: Scheduling the project meetings
o.C: Maintaining the integrity and traceability of test items, environments and testware versions
o.D: Purchasing cloud server instances

items.exEn: Configuration management makes results reproducible: every test knows which version of which item it ran against.

items.q: What is the main objective of a defect report?

o.A: Assigning blame to the developer responsible
o.B: Communicating the defect clearly enough for developers to reproduce, analyze and fix it
o.C: Justifying a request for a larger QA budget
o.D: Documenting the visual guidelines of the interface

items.exEn: A defect report is a communication tool; its value is measured by how easily the issue can be reproduced and fixed.

items.q: Which of the following information MUST be included in a well-written defect report?

o.A: Steps to reproduce, expected versus actual result, severity and environment details
o.B: A performance evaluation score for the developer
o.C: The full source code of the affected module
o.D: The roadmap of future features

items.exEn: Without reproduction steps and the expected/actual comparison, the report cannot be acted on reliably.

items.q: What is the difference between defect severity and defect priority?

o.A: Severity is the business urgency, while priority is the technical impact on the code
o.B: Severity is assigned by managers, while priority is assigned by developers
o.C: Severity is the degree of impact on the system, while priority is the urgency of fixing it from a business perspective
o.D: The two terms describe exactly the same thing

items.exEn: A defect can be highly severe but low priority, or cosmetic yet urgent — for example a misspelled company name on the home page.

items.q: Test monitoring involves which activity?

o.A: Taking corrective action when testing falls behind schedule
o.B: Continuously comparing actual progress against the plan using metrics
o.C: Redesigning the database schema
o.D: Authoring the original user requirements

items.exEn: Monitoring gathers and reports information; acting on that information is test control.

items.q: Test control refers to:

o.A: Measuring pass and fail execution ratios
o.B: Taking corrective actions to bring testing back on track based on monitoring information
o.C: Terminating the contracts of testers
o.D: Selecting the development tools for the team

items.exEn: Control is the reaction: re-prioritizing, re-allocating effort or adjusting the schedule when monitoring shows deviations.

items.q: Which estimation technique asks individual experts for estimates anonymously across several rounds until consensus is reached?

o.A: Function point analysis
o.B: Three-point estimation
o.C: Estimation based on lines of code
o.D: Wideband Delphi (and Planning Poker in Agile)

items.exEn: Wideband Delphi reaches a group estimate iteratively while limiting the influence of dominant participants.

items.q: In a test completion report, which key information should be presented to stakeholders?

o.A: The individual timesheets of the development team
o.B: The revision history of the source code
o.C: A summary of the testing performed, evaluation against the exit criteria, residual risks and key metrics
o.D: A price list of hardware components

items.exEn: The report supports a release decision: what was tested, what was found, and what risk remains.

items.q: Which of the following is a product risk rather than a project risk?

o.A: A key tester resigns during the peak of the execution phase
o.B: Delivery of the test environment hardware is delayed by the vendor
o.C: The QA budget is reduced by executive management
o.D: The software calculates incorrect interest rates for loan applications

items.exEn: An incorrect calculation is a defect in the delivered product, so it belongs to product risk.

items.q: Which role is responsible for creating test plans and test strategies?

o.A: The test manager (test lead)
o.B: The test execution engineer
o.C: The database administrator
o.D: The technical support specialist

items.exEn: The test manager owns planning, monitoring, control and reporting of the test effort.

items.q: Which of the following is a primary objective of test automation tools?

o.A: Increasing efficiency by automating repetitive tasks and regression suites
o.B: Completely replacing the need for human testers
o.C: Automatically eliminating all defects in production code
o.D: Making requirement specifications unnecessary

items.exEn: Tools support the process; they free tester time from repetitive execution rather than replacing testing itself.

items.q: What is a major risk associated with introducing test automation tools?

o.A: Test execution running too fast for the servers to handle
o.B: Unrealistic expectations about the tool's capabilities and the maintenance effort it requires
o.C: A reduction in the number of automated builds
o.D: Developers refusing to write production code

items.exEn: Automation has ongoing costs: scripts must be maintained as the product changes, and benefits take time to appear.

items.q: Which tool category supports static testing activities?

o.A: Static analysis tools and code linters
o.B: Performance testing tools
o.C: Test execution drivers
o.D: Network monitoring tools

items.exEn: Static analysis tools examine code and documents without executing them, often against coding standards.

items.q: Which tool category directly assists in test design and test case generation?

o.A: Defect tracking systems
o.B: Continuous integration servers
o.C: Model-based testing tools
o.D: Screen recording software

items.exEn: Model-based testing tools derive test cases automatically from a model of the expected system behavior.

items.q: What is a key benefit of using defect management tools?

o.A: Tracking the defect lifecycle, ownership and metrics across the whole team
o.B: Executing unit test scripts automatically
o.C: Generating API payloads for integration tests
o.D: Compiling the application source code

items.exEn: They keep the status, history and assignment of every defect visible, and produce the metrics used in reporting.

items.q: Which tool type simulates high user load in order to measure application response times?

o.A: Performance and load testing tools
o.B: Static analysis tools
o.C: Continuous integration servers
o.D: Defect tracking systems

items.exEn: Load and performance tools generate concurrent virtual users and measure response times and resource usage.

items.q: What does a test execution harness (test driver) do?

o.A: Reviews requirement documents for language errors
o.B: Executes tests automatically by calling the interfaces of the code under test and capturing the results
o.C: Generates user interface designs automatically
o.D: Monitors the physical temperature of the servers

items.exEn: A harness drives the component under test and compares actual results with expected ones.

items.q: What is a recommended practice when introducing a new tool into an organization?

o.A: Rolling the tool out to all projects at once without prior evaluation
o.B: Replacing the manual testing staff immediately
o.C: Running a proof of concept and a pilot project to assess how well the tool fits
o.D: Customizing the tool's source code before defining the requirements

items.exEn: A pilot verifies fit with the existing process, reveals the real effort needed and builds internal expertise.

items.q: Which tool type supports test management, requirement mapping and execution reporting?

o.A: Unit test frameworks
o.B: Test data generators
o.C: Test management tools
o.D: Static analysis linters

items.exEn: Test management tools hold the testware, link it to requirements, and record execution results and progress.

items.q: Dynamic analysis tools are used to:

o.A: Detect problems such as memory leaks and unhandled pointers while the code is running
o.B: Inspect requirement documents for missing descriptions
o.C: Design graphical wireframes
o.D: Conduct interviews with users

items.exEn: Dynamic analysis observes the software during execution to find defects that only appear at runtime.

items.q: What is a primary objective of dynamic test execution tools?

o.A: Running tests without needing an execution environment
o.B: Writing project status emails automatically
o.C: Automating repetitive execution steps in order to save execution time and effort
o.D: Managing employee payroll records

items.exEn: Execution tools repeat defined tests reliably, which is most valuable for regression cycles.

items.q: What is a potential risk of over-relying on automated test scripts?

o.A: High maintenance cost whenever the requirements or the interface change frequently
o.B: Automated scripts always run more slowly than manual testing
o.C: Test execution becomes completely unpredictable
o.D: Developers stop fixing defects

items.exEn: Automated scripts are software too: every change to the product may require updating them.

items.q: Which tool category is most useful for automated testing within a CI/CD pipeline?

o.A: Spreadsheet software used manually
o.B: Word processing software
o.C: Image editing tools
o.D: Build and deployment automation tools such as Jenkins or GitHub Actions

items.exEn: CI tools trigger the test suites automatically whenever code is committed, giving fast feedback on every change.

items.q: What role do test data generation tools play in testing?

o.A: They correct syntax errors in the code in real time
o.B: They create the realistic, high-volume datasets needed to execute test scenarios
o.C: They generate user story tickets for project managers
o.D: They configure the server hardware

items.exEn: Generating representative data at volume is often the slowest part of preparing an execution environment.

items.q: What is the primary criterion for selecting a test tool for an organization?

o.A: Choosing the most expensive tool on the market
o.B: How well the tool's capabilities match the organization's needs, technology stack and team skills
o.C: Choosing a tool that requires no training at all
o.D: Choosing a tool based on its visual appearance

items.exEn: Tool selection is a fit question: process, technology, budget, skills and support all weigh in.
